hypothesis: Removing live execution authority from only the SNDK and BRENTOIL commodity Swing routes, while preserving their observation and all Breakout routes, will improve stressed shared-portfolio behavior without broadly suppressing HIP-3 opportunity.
decision: Prepare an inactive v31 candidate whose only route-authority change is to remove SNDK and BRENTOIL from commodity Swing execution_symbols. Retain GOLD Swing, all commodity Breakout routes, every asset, both directions, risk, exits, and observation telemetry. Do not transition while positions are open and do not arm without explicit operator approval at a verified flat boundary.
falsifier: Reject or revise the candidate if source identities or common-clock replay fail to reproduce, if compatible forward or live evidence shows SNDK and BRENTOIL Swing positive across both directions under stressed costs, if missed opportunity exceeds avoided loss, or if the exact runtime authority differs from the tested config diff.
limitations: The common-clock windows are descriptive opened-window evidence rather than a sealed holdout.
Shared-capital route removal is path dependent and can expose displaced later entries.
Common-early coverage is sparse for narrower variants.
The candidate remains negative after removing its largest stressed winner.
Only four closed live HIP-3 lifecycles were available; open marks were excluded.
No live position, order, process, route authority, risk, exit, or TUI state changed.
